desc:
n seats are placed around a round table and numbered 0 to n - 1; seat i is next to seat i + 1, and seat n - 1 is next to seat 0. Choose exactly k seats so that no two chosen seats are neighbours. Seats are labelled, so a rotated choice is a different choice. Return the number of choices modulo 1,000,000,007.

n = 5, k = 2 -> 5   ({0,2}, {0,3}, {1,3}, {1,4}, {2,4})
n = 6, k = 2 -> 9
n = 6, k = 3 -> 2
hints: On a line, choosing k non-adjacent seats out of n is C(n - k + 1, k). The circle makes the first and last seats neighbours, which changes the count.
Count the chosen seats together with their gaps. Each chosen seat must be followed by at least one unchosen seat, so the gaps sum to n - k with every gap at least one.
The result is n / (n - k) * C(n - k, k). The quotient is an integer, so reduce it modulo the prime by multiplying with the inverse of n - k.
editorial: Fix a chosen seat and walk around the circle. The k chosen seats split the remaining n - k unchosen seats into k gaps, each of size at least one. Counting pairs (choice, marked chosen seat) gives k times the answer on one side and n times a composition count on the other, which yields n / k * C(n - k - 1, k - 1).
That is the same as n / (n - k) * C(n - k, k). For k = 0 the answer is 1 (the empty choice). For n = 5, k = 2 the formula gives 5 / 3 * C(3, 2) = 5.

Because n is up to 10<sup>9</sup> but k is at most 1,000, the binomial is a product of k terms times the inverse of k!, and the division by n - k uses a modular inverse. The constraint k ≤ n / 2 keeps n - k at least 1, so every inverse exists.
